title: 광노화에 따른 피부의 조직학적 변화
text: (논문 문단 그대로 복붙)

title: 광노화에 따른 피부의 조직학적 변화
text:
Population: 한국 성인 남성(20-85세)
Exposure/Condition: 연령 증가
Comparator: 연령대 간 비교
Outcome: epidermal_thickness (표피 두께)
Result: 연령 증가에 따라 표피 두께 감소 경향
Stats: p=0.017
Design: observational

title: 광노화에 따른 피부의 조직학적 변화
text: 이 연구는 한국인에서 나이가 증가할수록 표피 두께가 감소하는 경향을 관찰했다. 이는 피부 노화 과정에서 표피가 얇아질 수 있음을 시사한다.

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text: This study investigates how moderate-to-vigorous physical activity is associated with epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) using GrimAge, PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks in the Health and Retirement Study cohort followed from 2004 to 2016.

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text: Cross-sectional analyses in 2016 showed that physically active participants had significantly lower epigenetic age acceleration compared with inactive participants across GrimAge, PhenoAge and DunedinPACE measures.

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text: Structured life-course modelling identified both accumulation of physical activity and most recent activity (2016) as the strongest predictors of epigenetic age acceleration, indicating sustained and concurrent activity slow biological aging.

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text:
Population: US adults aged 56+
 Exposure: physically active vs inactive (PA-2016)
 Outcome: GrimAge acceleration
 Result: physically active participants had −1.26 years lower GrimAA (95% CI −1.59 to −0.93)
 Design: longitudinal observational

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text:
Population: US adults aged 56+
 Exposure: physically active vs inactive
 Outcome: PhenoAge acceleration
 Result: physically active participants had −1.70 years lower PhenoAA (95% CI −2.26 to −1.15)
 Design: longitudinal observational

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text:
Population: US adults aged 56+
 Exposure: physically active vs inactive
 Outcome: DunedinPACE (rate of biological aging)
 Result: physically active participants showed −0.05 lower aging rate per year (95% CI −0.06 to −0.04)
 Design: longitudinal observational

title: Physical Activity Is Associated With Decreased Epigenetic Aging
text: In a large US cohort followed for over a decade, people who engaged in regular moderate-to-vigorous physical activity showed slower biological aging measured by DNA methylation clocks. Both sustained activity over time and being active in later life were strongly linked to reduced epigenetic age acceleration.

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text: Cigarette smoke and solar rays are extrinsic exposome factors. Humans are rarely exposed to a single factor, so interactions (synergy) matter. This study evaluates chronic co-exposure (3% CSE + solar simulator light) on tissue-engineered bilayer skin substitutes reconstructed by the self-assembly method, and investigates skin-aging markers and mechanisms.

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text: Co-exposure with 3% CSE and 20 kJ/m2 UVA decreased living-epidermis thickness (p<0.05 vs control and 3% CSE alone) without affecting dermal thickness. Procollagen I synthesis decreased when 3% CSE was combined with SSL exposure (5/10/20 kJ/m2 UVA) to 0.5-fold (p<0.05), 0.2-fold (p<0.0001), and 0.05-fold (p<0.0001) vs control.

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text: MMP-1 activity was greater with combined extrinsic factors than alone (synergy). Collagen III and IV expression decreased when 3% CSE was combined with 10 and 20 kJ/m2 UVA. ERK1/2 phosphorylation ratio increased 3.4-fold (p<0.01) for 3% CSE + 20 kJ/m2 UVA; JNK showed a 3.3-fold increase trend (p<0.10).

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text:
Population/Model: healthy tissue-engineered bilayer skin substitutes (human keratinocytes+fibroblasts)
 Exposure: 3% cigarette smoke extract (CSE) once/day for 7 days + solar simulator light (SSL)
 Comparator: control; CSE alone
 Outcome: living_epidermis_thickness
 Result: co-exposure with 3% CSE + 20 kJ/m2 UVA decreased living epidermis thickness vs control and vs 3% CSE alone
 Stats: p<0.05
 Design: in_vitro_chronic_exposure

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text:
Population/Model: tissue-engineered skin substitutes
 Exposure: 3% CSE + SSL (UVA doses: 5, 10, 20 kJ/m2) once/day for 7 days
 Comparator: untreated control
 Outcome: procollagen_I_synthesis
 Result: fold-change vs control = 0.5 (5 kJ/m2; p<0.05), 0.2 (10 kJ/m2; p<0.0001), 0.05 (20 kJ/m2; p<0.0001)
 Design: in_vitro_chronic_exposure

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text:
Population/Model: dermis proteins extracted from skin substitutes
 Exposure: 3% CSE + UVA (10 or 20 kJ/m2)
 Comparator: untreated control; single-factor counterparts
 Outcome: collagen_III_expression; collagen_IV_expression
 Result: collagen III decreased to 0.4-fold for CSE+10 and CSE+20 (p<0.05). Collagen IV decreased to 0.3-fold (CSE+10) and 0.4-fold (CSE+20) (p<0.05).
 Design: in_vitro_chronic_exposure

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text:
Population/Model: epidermis proteins extracted from skin substitutes
 Exposure: 3% CSE + 20 kJ/m2 UVA
 Comparator: untreated control; other combinations; 20 kJ/m2 UVA alone
 Outcome: ERK1_2_phosphorylation; JNK_phosphorylation
 Result: p-ERK1/2 / ERK1/2 ratio increased 3.4-fold vs control (p<0.01) and vs 20 kJ/m2 UVA alone (p<0.05). JNK phosphorylation showed 3.3-fold increase trend vs control (p<0.10).
 Design: in_vitro_chronic_exposure

title: Scientific Reports (2023) 13:17969 (doi:10.1038/s41598-023-44868-z)
text: In a 3D reconstructed skin substitute model, chronic co-exposure to cigarette smoke extract (3% CSE) and solar simulator light produced synergistic skin-aging effects: reduced procollagen I synthesis and collagen protein expression, increased MMP activity, and activation of MAPK signaling (ERK1/2; JNK). The authors note that combining seemingly physiological daily doses can still cause deleterious skin-aging changes.

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text: This study examined whether objectively measured physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing and whether immune function and cardiovascular risk mediate this association. Using accelerometer-based activity data and DNA methylation clocks (GrimAge, PhenoAge, Hannum, Horvath), the authors analyzed adults from the Rhineland Study cohort in Germany.

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text: Higher daily step counts, greater energy expenditure (MET-hours), and a higher proportion of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity were non-linearly associated with lower GrimAge acceleration. For example, the difference in GrimAge acceleration between very inactive and average individuals corresponded to approximately 18–21 months of biological aging.

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text: Mediation analyses showed that part of the beneficial association between physical activity and slower epigenetic ageing was explained by improved cardiovascular risk profiles and immune function. Cardiovascular risk scores mediated up to ~50% of the association, whereas immune function mediated a smaller but significant proportion (~7%).

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text:
Population: community-dwelling adults (30–94 years)
 Exposure: higher vs lower physical activity (step counts, MET-hours)
 Outcome: GrimAge acceleration
 Result: individuals with average activity levels showed ~18–21 months lower GrimAge acceleration compared with very inactive individuals
 Design: cross-sectional observational

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text:
Population: community-dwelling adults
 Exposure: higher proportion of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity
 Outcome: GrimAge acceleration
 Result: higher MVPA associated with significantly slower epigenetic ageing; effect strongest at ~1.5 hours/day of MVPA
 Design: cross-sectional observational

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text:
Population: adults with cardiovascular data
 Exposure: physical activity level
 Mediator: Framingham risk score
 Outcome: GrimAge acceleration
 Result: cardiovascular risk mediated approximately 40–50% of the association between physical activity and slower epigenetic ageing
 Design: mediation analysis

title: Physical activity is associated with slower epigenetic ageing — Findings from the Rhineland study
text: In a large German population study, people who moved more in their daily lives showed slower biological ageing measured by DNA methylation clocks. Part of this benefit came from better heart health and stronger immune function. The findings suggest that staying physically active may help delay ageing at the molecular level.

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text: This review introduces the concept of the skin aging exposome, defined as the totality of non-genetic environmental factors contributing to extrinsic skin aging, including solar radiation, air pollution, cigarette smoke, nutrition, and climate factors. The authors emphasize that extrinsic skin aging results from the interaction of these exposomal factors with genetic background.

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text: The review summarizes evidence that ultraviolet radiation (UVB, UVA, especially UVA1), near-infrared radiation, and high-energy visible light contribute to extrinsic skin aging. Mechanisms include induction of oxidative stress, increased matrix metalloproteinase expression, reduced collagen synthesis, and altered pigmentation pathways.

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text: Epidemiological and mechanistic studies indicate that particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, and ozone contribute to extrinsic skin aging. These pollutants are linked to increased wrinkles and pigmentation through oxidative stress and collagen breakdown. Cigarette smoke further accelerates skin aging by upregulating MMP-1 and disturbing TGF-β signaling.

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
source_section: Dermal model of extrinsic skin aging
text: The authors propose a dermal-centered model of extrinsic skin aging in which chronic environmental exposures lead to accumulation of macromolecular damage, mitochondrial DNA mutations, and extracellular matrix degradation in dermal fibroblasts. These changes promote cellular senescence and drive long-term tissue aging.

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text:
Population: general population
 Exposure: chronic ultraviolet radiation (UVB, UVA, UVA1)
 Outcome: collagen degradation and wrinkle formation
 Result: UV exposure induces MMP-1, MMP-3, and MMP-9, reduces procollagen synthesis, and leads to cumulative collagen damage contributing to photoaging
 Design: narrative review of epidemiological and mechanistic studies

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text:
Population: urban-dwelling adults
 Exposure: particulate matter, NO2, ozone
 Outcome: skin pigmentation and wrinkle formation
 Result: air pollution associated with increased lentigines and wrinkles via oxidative stress and collagen metabolism disruption
 Design: narrative review of cohort, in vivo, and in vitro studies

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
source_section: Dermal model of extrinsic skin aging
text:
Population: human skin fibroblasts
 Exposure: chronic UV radiation and oxidative stress
 Outcome: mitochondrial DNA mutations and cellular senescence
 Result: repeated UV exposure increases large-scale mtDNA deletions in dermal fibroblasts, leading to reduced collagen synthesis and accelerated skin aging
 Design: narrative review of in vivo and in vitro studies

title: Environmentally-Induced Skin Aging: Exposomal Factors and Underlying Mechanisms
text: This review shows that skin aging is strongly shaped by our environment. Sunlight, air pollution, and smoking accelerate aging of the skin by damaging collagen, increasing oxidative stress, and promoting cellular senescence in the dermis. Reducing harmful exposures and protecting the skin may therefore help slow visible and biological skin aging.

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text: This study quantified how tobacco smoking affects the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs using the epigenetic clock method. DNA methylation data from buccal cells, airway cells, esophagus, and lung tissues were compared among non-smokers, smokers, and ex-smokers.

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text: Smoking significantly accelerated epigenetic aging in airway cells and lung tissue. Smokers showed higher epigenetic age acceleration compared with non-smokers, while buccal cells and esophagus tissue showed no significant acceleration.

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text: Smoking cessation significantly reduced epigenetic age acceleration in airway cells, bringing it close to levels observed in non-smokers. However, the accelerated aging in lung tissue was not significantly reversed after cessation.

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text:
Population: adult smokers vs non-smokers
 Exposure: tobacco smoking
 Outcome: epigenetic age acceleration in airway cells
 Result: smokers showed +4.9 years higher epigenetic age acceleration in airway cells
 Design: observational epigenetic study

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text:
Population: adult smokers vs non-smokers
 Exposure: tobacco smoking
 Outcome: epigenetic age acceleration in lung tissue
 Result: smokers showed +4.3 years higher epigenetic age acceleration in lung tissue (p=0.027)
 Design: observational epigenetic study

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text:
Population: ex-smokers vs smokers
 Exposure: smoking cessation
 Outcome: epigenetic age acceleration in airway cells
 Result: epigenetic aging rate significantly reduced after cessation (p=5.8×10−4)
 Design: observational epigenetic study

title: Effect of tobacco smoking on the epigenetic age of human respiratory organs
text: This study shows that smoking makes the airways and lungs biologically older than their actual age. Quitting smoking can slow or even reverse this aging effect in the airways, although damage in the lungs may be harder to undo. These findings provide strong evidence that stopping smoking can help preserve long-term respiratory health.

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text: This randomized intervention study investigated whether aerobic training (AT) and resistance training (RT) have different effects on skin aging in middle-aged women. While aerobic exercise is known to benefit skin, the effects of resistance training on skin aging had not been well characterized.

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
source_subsection: Effects of AT and RT on skin properties
text: Both aerobic and resistance training significantly improved skin elasticity and upper dermal structure after a 16-week intervention. However, only resistance training significantly increased dermal thickness, suggesting a unique effect of resistance exercise on age-related dermal thinning.

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text: Training interventions altered circulating inflammatory factors and increased the expression of dermal extracellular matrix-related genes in cultured human dermal fibroblasts. Resistance training specifically increased biglycan (BGN) expression, which is associated with dermal thickness.

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text: The study proposes that resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors such as CCL28 and CXCL4, thereby enhancing biglycan expression and increasing dermal thickness. These changes counteract age-related deterioration in dermal extracellular matrix.

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text:
Population: sedentary middle-aged Japanese women
 Intervention: aerobic training or resistance training for 16 weeks
 Outcome: skin elasticity
 Result: skin elasticity significantly improved in both AT and RT groups (p<0.001)
 Design: randomized intervention study

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text:
Population: sedentary middle-aged Japanese women
 Intervention: resistance training for 16 weeks
 Outcome: dermal thickness
 Result: dermal thickness significantly increased only in the RT group
 Design: randomized intervention study

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text:
Population: sedentary middle-aged Japanese women
 Intervention: resistance training
 Outcome: dermal thickness via biglycan expression
 Result: RT reduced circulating CCL28 and CXCL4, which suppress BGN expression; this led to increased dermal thickness
 Design: randomized intervention study with mechanistic analysis

title: Resistance training rejuvenates aging skin by reducing circulating inflammatory factors and enhancing dermal extracellular matrices
text: This study shows that exercise can make aging skin healthier. Both aerobic and resistance exercise improve skin elasticity, but resistance training has a special benefit: it makes the dermis thicker by reducing inflammation in the blood and increasing important skin-supporting proteins. Regular strength exercise may therefore help slow visible skin aging.

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text: This study investigates how alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde directly and indirectly affect human esophageal myofibroblasts (HEMFs) and epithelial cells. The authors examine how these exposures alter oxidative stress, inflammation, cell proliferation, and epithelial barrier integrity—mechanisms relevant to alcohol-related esophageal cancer risk.

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text: Direct exposure of HEMFs to alcohol and acetaldehyde increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, induced apoptosis at higher concentrations, and altered cytokine secretion. Low-dose acetaldehyde stimulated inflammatory mediators, whereas higher doses led to cytotoxicity.

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text: Supernatants from alcohol- or acetaldehyde-treated HEMFs altered esophageal epithelial cell behavior. Low concentrations increased epithelial proliferation, while higher concentrations reduced viability and disrupted epithelial scratch-wound closure, indicating indirect paracrine effects on tissue repair.

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text: The authors propose a model in which alcohol and acetaldehyde damage the esophageal microenvironment through both direct cytotoxic effects and indirect inflammatory signaling from myofibroblasts. This dual mechanism may explain how chronic alcohol exposure increases cancer susceptibility and impairs epithelial barrier function.

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text:
Population: human esophageal myofibroblasts (HEMFs)
 Exposure: acetaldehyde (30–40 µM)
 Outcome: oxidative stress and apoptosis
 Result: high-dose acetaldehyde significantly increased ROS and apoptotic cell death
 Design: in vitro experimental study

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text:
Population: human esophageal epithelial cells
 Exposure: supernatant from acetaldehyde-treated HEMFs
 Outcome: epithelial cell proliferation
 Result: low-dose acetaldehyde-treated HEMF supernatant increased epithelial proliferation up to ~2.4-fold
 Design: in vitro experimental study

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text:
Population: human esophageal epithelial cells
 Exposure: high-dose alcohol/acetaldehyde-treated HEMF supernatant
 Outcome: epithelial wound healing and barrier integrity
 Result: high-dose exposure reduced epithelial viability and delayed scratch-wound closure
 Design: in vitro experimental study

title: Direct and indirect effects of alcohol and its toxic metabolite acetaldehyde on human esophageal myofibroblasts and epithelial cells
text: This study shows that alcohol harms the cells of the esophagus in two ways. It directly damages cells by increasing oxidative stress, and indirectly worsens tissue health by triggering inflammatory signals from surrounding support cells. Together, these effects weaken the protective barrier of the esophagus and may raise the long-term risk of cancer.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
이 연구는 건강노화 지수를 통해 노인의 건강노화 수준을 평가하고 지역 간 차
 이를 비교하였으며, 건강노화에 영향을 미치는 개인 및 지역 수준의 요인을 규명하
 고자 하였다. 건강노화 지수는 건강노화 개념에 기반한 핵심 지표를 선정하여 산출
 하였다. 자료원으로는 2019년 지역사회건강조사에서 가져온 개인 수준 데이터를 
 사용하여 65세 이상 성인 72,660명의 단면 표본으로 구성하였다. 여기에 2019년 
 국가통계포털 지방지표 데이터에서 추출한 228개 지방자치단체(시·군·구)의 지역사
 회 수준 자료를 병합하였다. 건강노화 지수는 신체기능, 생리적 건강, 인지기능, 정
 신적 건강, 사회적 안녕의 다섯 가지 영역으로 구성하였다. 통계분석은 다층모형분
 석을 사용하였다. 건강노화 지수는 전국 시·군·구별로 뚜렷한 차이를 보였다. 서울
 특별시 서초구, 대전광역시 유성구 등은 높은 건강노화 지수를 보인 반면, 충청남
 도 서산시, 경기도 여주시 등은 낮았다. 개인 수준에서는 성별, 연령, 배우자 유무, 교육 수준, 월 가구 소득, 중등도 이상 신체활동, 음주, 흡연이 건강노화 지수와 유
 의한 관련성을 보였으며, 지역 수준에서는 노인여가복지시설 수가 건강노화와 긍정
 적인 관계를, 미충족 의료율은 부정적인 관계를 보였다. 개인 및 지역 수준 요인은 
 건강노화 지수의 75.8% 변동성을 설명하였다.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
건강노화 지수는 2019년 지역사회건강조사에 포함된 건강노화 관련 조사항목 
 및 측정도구를 활용하여 5개 영역으로 구성되었으며, 각 영역은 3개 문항으로 평
 가하여 0점에서 3점 사이로 산출하였다. 지수의 총점은 0점에서 15점점 사이로 점수
 가 높을수록 건강노화 수준이 높음을 의미한다(부록 표1). 
 첫째, 신체기능은 삶의 질 평가도구(Health Realted Quality of Life, EQ-5D)
 의 문항을 사용하여 운동능력, 자기관리 및 일상 활동 등에서 기능 제한 유무를 
 평가하였다.
 둘째, 생리적 건강은 만성질환 유무, 통증/불편감 유무, 그리고 주관적 구강건
 강 상태를 기준으로 평가하였다.
 셋째, 인지기능은 인지장애 경험 유무, 치매 선별검사 경험 유무 그리고, 집중력
 저하 경험 유무를 기준으로 평가하였다.
 넷째, 정신적 건강은 우울감 경험 유무, 주관적 스트레스 수준 및 삶의 만족도
 에 대한 세 가지 문항을 통해 평가하였다.
 마지막 다섯째는 사회적 안녕으로 사회적 관계, 사회활동 참여, 일의 여부를 평
 가하였다.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
연구 대상자는 총 72,660명으로, 건강노화 지수 평균은 9.93(±2.76)이었다. 중
 앙값은 10.0, 최빈값은 11.0으로 확인되었고, 건강노화 지수의 왜도는 -0.565, 첨
 도는 -0.238로, 분포는 정규성을 띠었다. 
 건강노화 지수는 지역별로 큰 차이를 보였다. 건강노화 지수가 높은 
 지역은 서울특별시의 서초구(10.93) 대전광역시 유성
 구(10.87)
반면, 건강노화 지수가 낮은 지역은 경기도 여주시(8.74) 충청남도 서산시(8.60)

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
모델 1인 기초모형에서 설명변수를 투입하지 않고 건강노화 지수의 지역 간 차
 이를 확인했다. 분석 결과, 지역 간 분산은 통계적으로 유의미했으며, ICC는 0.024
 로 나타나, 건강노화 지수의 전체 분산 중 약 2.4%가 지역 간 차이로 설명되었다.
 모델 3에서 개인 수준 변수에 지역 수준 변수를 추가하여 분석한 결과, 노인여
 가복지시설 비율이 건강노화 지수에 긍정적인 영향을 미쳤고, 미충족 의료율은 부
 정적인 영향을 미쳤다.
 임의효과 분석 결과 성별의 임의효과가 가장 높았으며(β
 =0.096, p<0.001), 개인 및 지역 수준 변수가 건강노화 지수 변동의 약 75.8%를 
 설명하였다.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인 (n=72,660)
 Exposure/Condition: 개인 특성(성별/연령/교육/소득/배우자) 및 건강행태(신체활동/음주/흡연), 지역 특성(미충족 의료율, 노인여가복지시설 등)
 Comparator: 개인/지역 특성 수준 간 비교
 Outcome: healthy_aging_index (건강노화 지수, HAI)
 Result: 2019년 지역사회건강조사 개인자료와 228개 지자체 지방지표를 병합해 건강노화 수준과 관련 요인을 분석.
 Stats: 다층모형분석(multilevel analysis)
 Design: 단면 2차자료 분석

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이

Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인 (n=72,660)

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인 (시·군·구 비교)
 Exposure/Condition: 거주 지역(시·군·구)
 Comparator: 지역 간 비교
 Outcome: healthy_aging_index (건강노화 지수, HAI)
 Result: HAI가 높은 지역 예: 서울 서초구(10.93), 대전 유성구(10.87). 낮은 지역 예: 충남 서산시(8.60), 경기 여주시(8.74).
 Stats: 지역별 평균 점수

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인 (228개 지자체)
 Exposure/Condition: 지역 수준(지자체) 변이
 Comparator: 지역 간
 Outcome: healthy_aging_index (건강노화 지수, HAI)
 Result: 기초모형에서 ICC=0.024로, HAI 분산의 약 2.4%가 지역 간 차이로 설명됨.
 Stats: ICC=0.024
 Design: 다층모형(기초모형)

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인
 Exposure/Condition: 중등도 이상 신체활동(실천)
 Comparator: 비실천
 Outcome: healthy_aging_index (건강노화 지수, HAI)
 Result: 다층모형(임의효과 포함)에서 신체활동은 HAI 증가와 관련(β=0.584).
 Stats: β=0.584, p<0.001
 Design: 단면(다층모형)

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text:
Population: 지역사회 거주 65세 이상 노인
 Exposure/Condition: 개인+지역 요인(성별/연령/소득/신체활동 등 + 지역 의료/복지 지표)
 Comparator: -
 Outcome: healthy_aging_index (건강노화 지수, HAI)
 Result: 개인 및 지역 수준 요인이 건강노화 지수 변동의 75.8%를 설명.
 Stats: Conditional R²=0.758
 Design: 다층모형

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text: 2019년 지역사회건강조사(65세 이상 72,660명)와 228개 지자체 지표를 합쳐 건강노화 지수(0~15점)를 만들고 지역 간 차이와 관련 요인을 분석했다. 전국 시·군·구별 건강노화 지수는 뚜렷하게 달랐고, 서초구·유성구 등은 높고 서산시·여주시 등은 낮았다. 다층모형에서 개인 요인(연령, 성별, 소득, 신체활동 등)과 지역 요인(미충족 의료율, 노인여가복지시설)이 함께 건강노화와 관련됐다.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text: 건강노화 지수는 신체기능, 생리적 건강, 인지기능, 정신적 건강, 사회적 안녕의 5개 영역을 각각 0~3점으로 채점해 합산(0~15점)했다. EQ-5D, PHQ-9 일부 문항, 만성질환 여부, 사회관계·사회활동·일 여부 등의 설문 항목을 사용했다.

title: 지역사회 노인의 건강노화 관련 요인 및 지역 간 차이
text: 기초모형에서 지역 간 차이는 전체 분산의 약 2.4%(ICC=0.024)로 작지만 유의했다. 개인 수준에서는 신체활동이 높고 흡연은 낮을수록 건강노화 지수가 높게 나타났다. 지역 수준에서는 미충족 의료율이 높을수록 건강노화 지수가 낮았다.
